tables.title: Blob use steps for modular exponentiation (CCOP = 0b01000101)
tables.text: Table 195, "Blob use steps for modular exponentiation (CCOP = 0b01000101)", in section 25.5.4 (RSA modular exponentiation) on page 766. Columns: OPSTEP, inM OPDKEA, iGn CSMAPEHS, Coupling or chaining operations, End-step (1)event, CPU action. 9 data row(s). Notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform described event for CCB to automatically go to the next step.; 2. SAES cannot be used for any operations, for security reasons.

rows:
–Enable the PKA in the correct mode, writing in 
PKA_CR MODE= 0x3 and EN=1 (repeat if EN bit 
stays clear). Wait for INITOK=1 in PKA_SR.
–Optionally decrypt blob encryption key in the SAES, 
using DHUK in 256-bit wrapped key mode.
–Set up AES-GCM in decryption mode with DHUK or 
the decrypted key in register (if applicable).
–Write operand A in the PKA RAM. Write constant K as 
operand A defined in Table194 when verifying the 
created blob.

–Complete GCM initialization in decryption mode, using 
saved random IV.
–Write reference tag in CCB_REFTAGR.

Write protected modular exponentiation parameters 
(PKA mode 0x3) in the PKA RAM, clearing CCF flags in 
the SAES, triggered after each-bitwrite.

–Write encrypted e in SAES_DINR, and runs AES 
decryption round.
–Write incrementally exponent e in the PKA, using 
0xCCB magic number. 
–Repeat for each 16-byte block of data.

–Write encrypted phi in SAES_DINR, and runs AES 
decryption round.
–Write incrementally phi in the PKA, using 0xCCB 
magic number. 
–Repeat for each 16-byte block of data.

–Complete GCM final.
–Read computed tag in the SAES (returns 0).

Start the operation in PKA setting START bit in 
PKA_CR.

The PKA computes the operation, PKA RAM is read as 
0.

eeRead A mod n in the PKA RAM. If the result is K mod 
n verify it matches the reference computed in Table194 
before saving the created blob in non-volatile memory.
notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform described event for CCB to automatically go to the next step.
2. SAES cannot be used for any operations, for security reasons.
